content:
We need number of CH3 groups in the molecule. But we have no description of molecule. Possibly we need to get NMR spectra and infer number of methyl groups. Could use proton NMR to count methyl signals (singlet, doublet, etc). But we don't have SMILES. The sample is "at hand". Likely the system has a sample loaded. We can request proton NMR spectra. That will show peaks; methyl groups appear around 0.9 ppm (alkyl) or 2.0 (next to carbonyl). Counting distinct methyl signals may be ambiguous. But maybe the molecule is simple and the number of methyl groups equals number of peaks in the 1H NMR that integrate to 3H. However integration not given.

Alternative: Use carbon NMR; methyl carbons appear around 10-30 ppm. Counting distinct methyl carbon signals.

Simplify: Use carbon NMR and count signals in that region.

We can request carbon NMR spectra.
